paper_metadata.title: End-to-end resource analysis for quantum interior point methods and portfolio optimization

summary: The paper performs a full circuit‑level resource analysis of a quantum interior point method for portfolio optimization and estimates that solving an instance with n=100 assets would require about 8×10^6 logical qubits, ~7×10^29 T gates, and ~2×10^24 T‑depth. Numerical simulations of small instances (n≤120) show condition numbers around 1.6×10^4 and algorithmic scaling roughly O(n^3.5), leading the authors to conclude that practical quantum advantage is unlikely without major algorithmic improvements.

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum interior point method (QIPM) for second-order cone programming applied to portfolio optimization, including numerical simulation of small portfolio instances and resource estimation for fault-tolerant gate-based quantum circuits.

algorithm.variant: Quantum interior point method with quantum linear system solver (QLSS); infeasible QIPM (II-QIPM) with self-dual embedding and adiabatic QLSS
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate until duality gap µ < ϵ; in resource estimates ϵ = 10^-7 for n = 100

hyperparameters.tomography_precision_adaptive: xi halved until central-path neighborhood condition satisfied

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start on self-dual central point (x=e, y=0, τ=1, θ=1, s=e, κ=1)

optimizer_settings.step_size: chosen to reduce duality gap by factor sigma each iteration

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio optimization is reduced to SOCP with variables x=(w, ϕ, ρ, t, η) and self-dual embedding; Newton linear systems are solved via QLSS. No QUBO/binary encoding is used.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w -u_hat^T w + q*sqrt(w^T Sigma w) subject to 1^T w = 1, |w - w_bar| <= zeta, w >= 0
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: SOCP constraints with self-dual embedding; feasibility maintained approximately in II-QIPM; tomography precision adaptively chosen to stay in central-path neighborhood; simple row-normalization preconditioning

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on randomly chosen stocks from the Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (DWCF), using historical returns to build covariance and mean return estimates.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (DWCF)

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock returns; example uses n=30 stocks and first m=60 days; resource estimate uses n=100

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute average return vector u_hat and covariance matrix Sigma from historical returns; choose M such that Sigma = M^T M using returns over m epochs; set current portfolio w_bar proportional to market capitalization; q=1; zeta=0.05*1
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation of full QIPM; 128 random portfolio samples for each n; scaling fits on log-log plots; median and percentile bands reported; adaptive tomography precision and central-path neighborhood checks

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Adaptive tomography precision; simple preconditioning; no hardware noise model or mitigation on QPU reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical exact linear solver used only in numerical simulation of the quantum subroutine; ECOS/classical IPM discussed as baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct SOCP from portfolio optimization; compute M, A, b, c; row-normalize Newton matrix; precompute block-encoding angles and QSP phases classically
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Tomography converts quantum state to classical estimate of Newton step; update IPM iterate classically; return x/tau

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: duality gap decreases exponentially with iterations; tomography precision plateaus in simulations

classical_baselines.method_name: classical interior point method with Gaussian elimination
classical interior point method with fast matrix multiplication

speedup_claims.factor: up to O(L) quantum advantage in linear-system solving when kappa_F ∝ L and xi = O(1)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical linear-system solvers (Gaussian elimination and randomized Kaczmarz)
speedup_claims.conditions: for linear systems; if kappa_F scales linearly with L and tomography precision is constant
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states this is only a limited asymptotic advantage and that practical advantage is unlikely due to large constants and tomography overhead.

speedup_claims.conditions: n up to 120 in simulations; n=100 resource estimate
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper concludes no practical quantum advantage is shown; resource counts are prohibitively large.

speedup_claims.factor: if tomography were improved to O(L log L / xi), runtime would scale as n^1.5 kappa_F / xi
speedup_claims.conditions: hypothetical replacement with newer tomography method from Ref. [34]
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a projected improvement only; additional gate overhead would be introduced.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(k * Nit * kappa_F * L * sqrt(r) * xi^-2 * polylog(L,1/epsilon)) in leading-order resource expressions; table VI gives T-depth ~ (5e8) kappa_F L sqrt(r) xi^-2 log2(epsilon^-1) log2(L) log2(kappa_F L^(14/27) xi^-1)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical IPM with Gaussian elimination: O(n^3.5) for the PO formulation; randomized Kaczmarz baseline O(L kappa_F^2 log(xi^-1)) for linear systems
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Very large; e.g. QLSS prefactor ~1.31*2305 and full QIPM leading constants in tables VI/X
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: Gaussian elimination prefactor mild; randomized Kaczmarz prefactor about 8 in table XI
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: At n=100, about 6e12 circuit repetitions and 3e8 tomography repetitions per QLSS run; full QIPM about 3e12 classical repetitions of quantum circuits plus controlled versions
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: PO problem solvable in seconds on a laptop for n=100; classical IPM O(n^3.5) or better with fast matrix multiplication
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: Millions of years for 10^24 T-depth at gigahertz clock rates; with hypothetical 4GHz QRAM still ~10,000 years for n=100
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: Seconds on a laptop for n=100

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not identified; classical solves n=100 instances in seconds while the quantum estimate requires ~8×10^6 logical qubits and ~2×10^24 T-depth.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Paper estimates ~8×10^6 logical qubits, ~7×10^29 T gates, and ~2×10^24 T-depth for n=100 with ~6×10^12 circuit repetitions.
limiting_factors: Huge T-depth dominated by QLSS calls and tomography repetitions
Tomography cost scaling as O(L log L / ξ^2)
Very large constant factors in QLSS implementation

notes: hardware.type is not specified because the paper is a resource analysis and does not report execution on a specific QPU or simulator
num_qubits, T-depth, and T-count are explicitly reported in tables I, VI, and X

speedup_order is inferred from the paper's conclusion that no practical advantage is found and asymptotic speedup is not established; the paper states the outlook is pessimistic and 'neither do they definitively rule it out'

The authors explicitly conclude the outlook for practical quantum advantage is pessimistic and that classical methods solve the n=100 problem in seconds while the quantum algorithm would take millions of years at GHz clock rates.

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of the feasible inexact‑feasible quantum interior point method (IF‑QIPM) for portfolio optimization using a hand‑constructed null‑space basis for feasibility constraints.

algorithm.key_quantum_component: Quantum linear system solver with tomography

key_results: Simulated convergence of IF‑QIPM on portfolios up to n=120 assets.
Observed condition number scaling approximately κ_F ∼ n^(0.57–1.01) depending on duality gap.
Tomography precision scaling approximately ξ^-2 ∼ n^(−0.01 to 0.93) with large variance.

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of the feasible QIPM variant using QR decomposition to compute the null‑space basis (IF‑QIPM‑QR).

algorithm.variant: Feasible quantum interior point method with QR‑based null‑space basis (IF‑QIPM‑QR)
algorithm.key_quantum_component: Quantum linear system solver with tomography

key_results: Empirical condition number scaling κ_F ∼ n^(0.23–0.98) depending on duality gap.
Algorithm scaling approximately O(n^3.5) for median instances at small duality gap.
Better empirical stability than IF‑QIPM but requires costly classical QR decomposition.
